title: How would you design a system to send 1 million (or 100M) push notifications without overwhelming your servers: decouple generation from delivery via a queue, scale a worker fleet independently by queue depth, rate-limit to the provider (e.g. Firebase), make processing idempotent (unique notification ID), use provider batch APIs (1 request → N notifications), add retries → DLQ, generate campaign jobs progressively at very large scale, and track delivery through async provider callbacks?
shortTitle: How would you design a system to send 1 million (or 100M) push notifications without overwhelming your servers
keyPoints: Decouple generation from delivery with a durable queue: the generator enqueues, workers drain at a sustainable rate.
Autoscale the delivery fleet by queue depth so servers are never overwhelmed by bursty generation.
Rate-limit outbound calls with a token bucket sized to the provider's allowed rate (Firebase, APNs).
Make each notification idempotent with a unique ID so at-least-once delivery becomes effectively exactly-once.
Use provider batch APIs so one request delivers to many devices, dramatically reducing outbound calls.
Progressive campaign generation paginates the recipient set in chunks to keep the queue bounded.
Track delivery through async provider callbacks, updating each notification's state by unique ID.

s1_definition.oneliner: Send notifications at scale by decoupling generation from delivery with a queue, autoscaling workers by queue depth, rate-limiting and batching to the provider, and making each notification idempotent by unique ID.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Decouple** – A generator enqueues notification jobs; a separate worker fleet drains them at a sustainable rate. The queue is the shock absorber.
- **Autoscale** – Workers scale by queue depth: add when the backlog grows, remove when it drains.
- **Rate limit** – A token bucket on the outbound path ensures the fleet never exceeds the provider's allowed rate.
- **Idempotency** – Each notification has a unique ID; reprocessed jobs check and skip if already sent.
- **Batch API** – One request to Firebase carries hundreds of device tokens, reducing outbound calls dramatically.
- **Progressive generation** – For 100M recipients, paginate and enqueue in chunks rather than materializing all at once.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India must text 100 million customers about a new scheme. If one clerk tried to call everyone at once, the branch collapses. Instead, one team writes names onto slips and drops them into a big in-tray (queue), and a separate team of senders takes slips and sends at a steady pace the phone network accepts. Each slip has a unique ticket number so nobody is messaged twice. The name-writers work through the list in chunks. Delivery confirmations arrive later and are ticked off.

sections.s6_takeaway:
To send 100 million push notifications without overwhelming servers, the single most important decision is decoupling generation from delivery with a durable queue. At National Bank of India, an early attempt generated and sent synchronously, instantly overwhelming the senders and getting the system throttled by Firebase, with duplicate sends annoying customers after worker crashes.

Pankaj rebuilt it as a pipeline: a progressive generator feeding a partitioned Kafka queue in 10,000-recipient chunks, an autoscaled worker fleet that batched 500 device tokens per Firebase multicast request under a token-bucket rate limiter, a unique notification ID so reprocessed jobs skipped already-sent messages, and a dead-letter queue for invalid tokens that also fed token cleanup. After that, a 100-million campaign became a smooth background job that scaled the fleet up and back down.

Delivery tracking used Firebase's async callbacks, updating each notification's state (sent, delivered, opened, failed) by unique ID, giving precise campaign metrics without the send path ever blocking on confirmation. The nuance Pankaj adds is keeping a separate priority topic so time-critical OTPs are never stuck behind a marketing blast.

Remember one sentence: Decouple generation from delivery with a queue, autoscale workers by depth, rate-limit and batch to the provider, make each notification idempotent by unique ID, generate progressively, and track delivery via async callbacks.
